This document describes how we map the checklist data to Darwin Core.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

Load libraries:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(janitor)
library(readxl)
library(digest)
```

# Read source data

Read source data:
 
```{r}
raw_data <- read_excel(path = here("data", "raw", "checklist_update_2025.xlsx")) 
```

Preview raw data:

```{r}
glimpse(raw_data)
```

# Create version 2.0

First clean-up of the data:

```{r}
input_data <- raw_data %>% clean_names()
```

Define look-up table for native ranges:

```{r}
lookup <- c(
      "AF" = "Africa",
      "AM" = "pan-American",
      "AS" = "Asia",
      "AS-Te" = "temperate Asia",
      "AS-Tr" = "tropical Asia",
      "AUS" = "Australasia",
      "Cult." = "cultivated origin",
      "E" = "Europe",
      "Hybr." = "hybrid origin",
      "NAM" = "Northern America",
      "SAM" = "Southern America",
      "Trop." = "Pantropical")
```



```{r}
vdigest <- Vectorize(digest)

input_data <- input_data |>
  mutate(`taxonID hash` = vdigest(taxon, algo = "md5"),
         `scientific name` = taxon,
         kingdom = "Plantae",
         `nomenclatural code` = "ICN",
         `country code` = "BE",
         
      # Change `X`,`?` and NA to numerical values to calculate the total number of regions where a taxon occurs
         `presence Flanders` = case_when(
           presence_fl =="X" ~ "1",
           is.na(presence_fl) ~ "0",
           .default = "?"),
         `presence Wallonia` = case_when(
           presence_wa =="X" ~ "1",
           is.na(presence_wa) ~ "0",
           .default = "?"),
         `presence Brussels` = case_when(
           presence_br =="X" ~ "1",
           is.na(presence_br) ~ "0",
           .default = "?"),

      # Calculate the total number of region where a taxon occurs
         `nr of regions` = rowSums(
           cbind(
             as.numeric(na_if(`presence Flanders`, "?")),
             as.numeric(na_if(`presence Wallonia`, "?")),
             as.numeric(na_if(`presence Brussels`, "?"))
           ),
           na.rm = TRUE),
      
      # Determine whether a species is present in Belgium or not:
         `occurrence status` = case_when(
           
           # If the total number of regions is not zero, the species is certainly present in Belgium 
           `nr of regions` != 0 ~ "present",
    
           
           # If the total number of regions is zero, it's only 100% certain that it's absent if it's absent in all regions
           `presence Flanders` == "0" & `presence Wallonia` == "0" & `presence Brussels` == "0" ~ "absent",
           .default = "presence uncertain"),
  
           
         `establishment means` = "introduced",
         `degree of establishment` = case_when(
           d_n == "Nat." | d_n == "Nat.?" ~ "established",
           d_n == "Cas."| d_n == "Cas.?" ~ "casual",
           d_n == "Inv." ~ "invasive",
           .default = as.character(d_n)),
         `introduction pathway 1` = NA_character_,
         `introduction pathway 2` = NA_character_,
         `introduction pathway 3` = NA_character_,
         `date first observation` = str_replace_all(fr, "(\\?|ca. |<|>)", ""),
         `date last observation` = str_replace_all(mrr, "(\\?|ca. |<|>)", ""),
         `source` = NA_character_,
         `occurrence remarks` = NA_character_,
         `native range` = str_replace_all(origin, lookup),
         `native range` = str_replace_all(`native range`, "\\s+", " | "),
         terrestrial = case_match(habitat,
                                  "Terrestrial" ~ TRUE,
                                  "terrestrial" ~ TRUE,
                                  "Terrestrial/fresh water" ~ TRUE,
                                  .default = FALSE),
         freshwater = case_match(habitat,
                                 "Terrestrial/fresh water" ~ TRUE,
                                 "Fresh water" ~ TRUE,
                                 .default = FALSE),
         `date added` = NA_character_
         )
         
         
```

Put all columns in order and rearrange:

```{r}
input_data <-
  input_data %>% select(
    `taxonID hash`, scientific_name_id, `scientific name`, hybrid_formula,
    kingdom, family, taxon_rank, `nomenclatural code`,
    `presence Flanders`,`presence Wallonia`, `presence Brussels`, `nr of regions` ,`country code`,
    `occurrence status`, 
    `establishment means`, d_n ,`degree of establishment`,
    m_i, v_i, `introduction pathway 1`, `introduction pathway 2`, `introduction pathway 3`,
    fr, `date first observation`,
    mrr, `date last observation`,
    source,
    origin, `native range`,
    habitat, terrestrial, freshwater,
    `date added`)
```

Export as .csv:


```{r}
write_csv(input_data, here("data", "raw", "raw_new.csv"), na = "")

```
